title: Snapshot-driven UX heuristics and variant guardrails for Cost Explorer and Rollouts
creator: Aisha Moreno
summary: Introduce a snapshot-driven heuristics layer and variant guardrails that let Cost Explorer panels and rollout controls automatically adjust density, legend verbosity, and component variants based on recent metric distributions and active rollout states.
background: We regularly get feedback that cost dashboards become noisy or sparse depending on the slice of traffic and on which rollout is active. Designers and engineers currently maintain separate density decisions in each component (cards, sparklines, legends, rollout controls). This ticket proposes a small, centralized heuristics pattern that consumes a recent metrics snapshot (percentiles, peak rate, anomaly flags, active rollout variant) and outputs UI signals: density token, legend verbosity, and variant lock state.
goals: 1) Create a consistent UX mechanism so Cost Explorer, per-model cost cards, and rollout rails present coherent density and legend states across views. 2) Reduce ad-hoc per-component overrides and duplicated logic. 3) Ship a prototype in Figma + a handoff spec for frontend implementers. 4) Validate with performance and accessibility audits.
scope: Design tokens and patterns for density and legend verbosity; a small new Snapshot Badge component; mapping tables and a handoff document for engineers. Produce Figma prototypes for desktop and compact mobile. Include acceptance criteria and QA checklist.
out_of_scope: Backend snapshot ingestion pipeline (data infra), rollout server-side logic, and Dedicated capacity billing engine. Those will be integrated via an agreed contract but are not implemented here.
success_metrics: Design consistency: Reduce manual variance overrides in Cost Explorer components by 80% (tracked via a frontend lint rule after implementation)
User clarity: In a 5-task usability study, reduce time-to-find-cost-peak by 20% for new users
Developer ergonomics: Handoff reduces front-end estimated effort for density changes by 40% (survey of 3 eng teams)
Accessibility: All new tokens pass color-contrast >= 4.5:1 for text elements
constraints: Must work with existing token system and not require wholesale renaming
Figma prototypes should be built from existing component library instances where possible
Behavior must be definable by a simple JSON output from the backend (three signals max: density, legend_verbosity, variant_lock)
Low-runtime overhead: front-end should be able to compute final state with O(1) checks once snapshot signals are available
proposed_design: Introduce a Snapshot Heuristics spec + a small Snapshot Badge component that surfaces the heuristic state for debugging. Heuristics map percentile ranges and anomaly flags to three discrete density tokens (compact / comfortable / spacious) and two legend verbosity levels (summary / detailed). For rollout controls we add a variant_guardrail flag: when true, components render the canonical variant (no local overrides) and a subtle lock icon appears in the rollout rail. All mappings are captured in a single handoff table and an adapter component will expose a single 'uiState' prop to downstream components.
token_changes: Legend: legend.verbosity.summary and legend.verbosity.detailed token rules (line-height, truncation thresholds)
Icon token: snapshot.badge.lock with 12px vs 16px variants
components_touched: Legend component used across dashboard cards
